SILT#00078: Up until the 1970s, we could have assigned every person a unique 32-bit number as an ID (assuming it rotated when someone dies). If we want to do the same nowadays, we would only need at most 2 extra bits (possibly even 1 at time of writing). I'm not sure why this makes 2^32 feel small
